title.en: Compare radio waves, microwaves and infrared

say.en: Your TV remote, your FM radio and the dish on a rooftop all send data without wires, but they use very different waves. Why can't a TV remote work from another room? In this lesson: Compare radio waves, microwaves and infrared.
Describe Bluetooth and Wi-Fi WLAN.

body.en: *Radio waves* (about 3 kHz – 1 GHz) are omnidirectional, travel long distances and can pass through walls; they are used in AM/FM radio, cordless phones and mobile communication. Microwaves (about 1 GHz – 300 GHz) are unidirectional and need line of sight; they cannot pass through solid objects and are used for satellite and point-to-point tower links. Infrared waves (about 300 GHz – 400 THz) work only over very short distances, need line of sight and cannot pass through walls; they are used in TV remotes.

points.en: Microwave: line of sight, satellite and tower links

narration.en: Radio waves spread everywhere and pass through walls. Microwaves need a straight line of sight. Infrared is very short range and cannot pass through walls.
narration.kn: ರೇಡಿಯೋ ತರಂಗಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲ ದಿಕ್ಕಿಗೆ ಹರಡಿ ಗೋಡೆ ದಾಟುತ್ತವೆ. ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ತರಂಗಗಳಿಗೆ ನೇರ ದೃಷ್ಟಿರೇಖೆ ಬೇಕು. ಅವಗೆಂಪು ಅತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ದೂರ, ಗೋಡೆ ದಾಟದು.

title.en: On the board: The wireless spectrum

say.en: Wireless media use electromagnetic waves. We order them by frequency.
Radio waves, from 3 kilohertz to 1 gigahertz, spread in all directions and pass through walls: FM radio and mobile phones.
Microwaves, 1 to 300 gigahertz, go in one direction and need line of sight: satellite and tower links.
Infrared, 300 gigahertz to 400 terahertz, works only over a short distance and cannot pass walls: TV remotes.
Bluetooth links devices within about 10 metres at 2.4 gigahertz: one primary and up to seven active secondaries form a piconet.

body.en: Bluetooth is a short-range *wireless* technology (about 10 m) working at 2.4 GHz that connects devices like phones, earbuds and keyboards; a Bluetooth network (piconet) has one primary device and up to seven active secondary devices. A wireless LAN (WLAN, Wi-Fi) connects devices within a building through access points connected to the wired network.

problem.en: Choose a wireless medium for: (i) a TV remote, (ii) linking two towers 30 km apart with a clear line of sight, (iii) a city FM station, (iv) wireless earbuds.

steps.en: (i) Very short range, same room → infrared.
(ii) Long point-to-point link with line of sight → microwave.
(iii) Must reach every home, through walls → radio waves.
(iv) Personal devices within a few metres → Bluetooth.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Choose a wireless medium for: (i) a TV remote, (ii) linking two towers 30 km apart with a clear line of sight, (iii) a city FM station, (iv) wireless earbuds.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Choose a wireless medium for: i a TV remote, ii linking two towers 30 kilometres apart with a clear line of sight, iii a city FM station, iv wireless earbuds.
i Very short range, same room gives infrared.
ii Long point-to-point link with line of sight gives microwave.
iii Must reach every home, through walls gives radio waves.
iv Personal devices within a few metres gives Bluetooth.
So the answer is i infrared, ii microwave, iii radio, iv Bluetooth.
